newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - IBP to buy Foodbrands America for $640 million.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - IBP to buy Foodbrands America for $640 million.

text.p: Giant meat processor IBP Inc., seeking to tap into the growing market for foods prepared away from home, said Wednesday it agreed to acquire Foodbrands America Inc., a food service supplier, in a $640 million deal.
IBP, based on Dakota City, Neb., said it bid $23.40 a share for Foodbrands, for a total of $292 million in cash, and will assume about $348 million in Foodbrands' debt.
Foodbrands stock on the New York Stock Exchange jumped $7.375 a share to $23.125 after the deal. The stock of IBP, the nation's largest meatpacker, gained 62.5 cents to $25.625.

Oklahoma City-based Foodbrands is the leader in the pizza toppings industry and also produces more than 1,600 branded and custom products from pizza crust and burritos to soups, sauces and stuffed pasta. Its customers include restaurant chains, food service distributors, warehouse clubs and grocery store delicatessens in the United States and Europe.
For IBP, based in Dakota City, Neb., the acquisition will advance its steps toward diversifying into food service and other value-added, premium-priced food products.

"Food prepared outside of the home accounts for over 50 percent of food purchases and is responsible for most of the food industry sales growth," Larry Shipley, IBP's executive vice president, corporate development, said in an interview.

IBP has been making its own strides toward value-added products, including more "butcher friendly" trimmed meats for grocery stores, pre-cooked pizza toppings and taco fillings, and entrees for food service, Shipley added.
"I would expect that by the year 2000, somewhere between 8 and 12 percent of IBP's sales and revenue will be accounted for by these value-added products," Shipley said.
In a statement, IBP Chairman Robert Peterson said IBP's fresh beef and pork already reach supermarket cases, restaurants and food service companies all over the world.

"The addition of Foodbrands' business is a perfect complement to IBP's core processing business and will allow us to further extend our reach into restaurants and supermarket deli cases with high quality branded products," Peterson added.
Analysts applauded the acquisition, saying it will move IBP more into food service and lessen somewhat its reliance on the cyclical meat processing business.
"It moves them up the value chain to add value to their commodity products," Natwest analyst David Nelson said.
Piper Jaffray analyst George Dahlman said he considered Foodbrands to be the best choice for IBP to expand in the food service arena.

"If you were to tell me that IBP was changing its stripes and would focus more on value-added products in food service, the first (acquisition target) that would have come to mind would be Foodbrands," Dahlman said.
"What Tyson is to chicken, IBP hopes to be to beef and pork," Prudential analyst John McMillin added, referring to Tyson Foods Inc., the chicken processor that sells fresh and cooked poultry.
IBP said it would begin a cash tender offer for all of Foodbrands stock on April 1. It added that Foodbrands' three biggest stockholders had agreed to tender their shares.

IBP said it intended to operate Foodbrands, which has 3,300 employees, as a largely independent business. Randolph "Randy" Devening, Foodbrands chairman, will stay on to run that business, Shipley said.
The transaction had been approved by the boards of both companies and is expected to close by the end of June, subject to certain regulatory approvals.
